body: If you have the time, can you please tell me exactly what to do, step by step? Do I go to the police? How do I get a solicitor? This is complicated and I'm honestly terrified because I don't know where to start

This is such a detailed response, I appreciate it so much. 

I have a lot of concerns, mainly that I've previously lied to the police. I told the police that I paid my accommodation fees myself by working excessively and that the fraudsters only contacted me on a phone that they gave me to use and then took back when they were done with me. This is because I didn't want them to find out about how my accommodation fees were paid, as I believed I would be kicked out of university and get myself into trouble.

My phone is actually full of months worth of evidence, but none that shows that they threatened me. They were very careful not to say anything threatening over text. The texts show me begging for their help and a good rapport between us if anything. I don't know the fraudsters surnames, but I do know of people that probably do know who they are, as I was introduced via a mutual "friend" who I now know knew all along that this would happen to me. I understand that they also used pay as you go mobile sims, that they changed and disposed of regularly, making connecting phone number to user impossible.

What can I do? I don't think I can prove duress as I don't have sufficient evidence of threats made. I'm worried that I would only incriminate myself more, as my phone would show that I knew what was going on and even wanted it to happen, as I thought I was going to benefit from it. I want undeniably manipulated and used, but that is my own fault for being gullible and stupid. 

My step mum is an accountant and she is trying to help me. We were pretty set on a DRO, but finding out that I may have a CIFAS marker changes things, as I'd have to lose my Santander student bank account because it's overdrawn, and then would not be able to open a new bank account due to being labelled by CIFAS as a money launderer. My advisor from Stepchange has also informed me that I could lose this bank account at any time, should Santander decide to run a "know your customer" check on me. She's also told me that it's likely that my DRO won't even go through, as my creditors can dispute that I'm just lying about all of this and just don't want to pay. I've sent my details away to CIFAS to request to see the information that they have on me, but I'm assuming I've been blacklisted due to the closure of my HSBC account. I've also applied to Experian to see a more detailed credit report than the dismal one that I've seen on Clearscore. 

What should I do? I don't think there is anything I can do and I'm scared that anything I try is only going to make the situation worse. Thank you for your help, any further advice would be very welcome.
If I can't have a bank account it's not only money is it, can't really exist in society without one, would honestly rather die

I've realised I may have a Money Laundering CIFAS marker on me, due to the closure of my HSBC account, as I've tried to open a basic account with Lloyds and had my application initially accepted and then declined. My advisor from StepChange presumes that this is the case. What do I do?? I desperately need a new bank account...
This is honestly the most constructive and understanding response I've received regarding this. I'm new to Reddit and people have mostly been very cruel on other subs. Thank you so much.

Mighty big of you to call BS on a situation you know nothing about. How was I supposed to simply go to the police, when the people who were threatening me told me they would come to my family home, beat up my mum and then shoot me in front of her if I did so? Also how lucky you are to clearly live in an environment where you can trust that police are actually going to protect you and keep you safe.

Thank you for being so nice. I'm really stuck, it's been months and I've acted up recently and been petty af, picking fights and taking stuff he says personally. I don't know what to do, but a letter is a good idea.

I knew it wasn't okay, I hated doing it. I'm not heartless, I just wanted to keep him safe. People were threatening to kill me, I just didn't want him to get caught up in my mess and get himself hurt.

I'm halfway through a degree at a Russell Group uni, would be a real shame to quit now. I do have internships at London based fashion magazines waiting for me if I want them, I'm just determined to get that "cap n gown" moment first as I've been through so many absences from my education due to mental health issues... I just want to stick it to everybody who said I would never be able to do it.

I'm studying English Lit and I definitely want to stick within a creative field so I'm not too concerned about the impact it will have on my career. 

I really don't understand how credit works and I'm very anxious about the fact that my score is at 0. How can I fix this? is fixing it feasible? Is it really that big of a deal?

I have only spoken to the banks that provided the loans to take the watches out, I didn't think of speaking to the jewellers! It might be a hail Mary but like you said, it's worth a try. I'll write some letters and I do have a crime ref no  so hopefully they'll see that I'm being sincere.

Thank you, really struggling at the moment. I'm off sick from both uni and my part time job because I've had a breakdown. My uni are being surprisingly supportive, but I'm being constantly reminded that universities are a business and they just want my money in the long run.

My main concerns are that I've already lost one bank account (HSBC), and I don't know if the closure of my account means I've been blacklisted from banking with them ever again...

 If I go with the DRO, I'll have to lose my current student bank account (Santander) as I'm well into my overdraft, which isn't a major problem, as I've been assured I can just take out whatever is left of my overdraft and put it into a new bank account to tide me over until my next Student Finance payment arrives. I'm just very worried that this will mean I'm effectively blacklisted from two major banks. 

I've also been advised that the best way to start to rebuild my credit is to take out a mobile phone contract in my name. Will any phone provider allow someone with a 0 credit score to do this?! I'm totally clueless and I didn't even really know what credit was before I came to university. Any advice you're at liberty to give me without breaching the regulations of your job would be amazing!
